 IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EL                                )
 PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR REVISION OF                                 )
 ITS RETAIL ELECTRIC RATES,                                            ) Docket No. 25-00082-UT
 EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY,                                             )
 Applicant.                                                            )

                          ORDER GRANTING EXTENSION OF TIME

         THIS MATTER comes before the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) upon El Paso Electric Company’s (“EPE”) Unopposed And Verified Motion For

Variance Regarding Rate Case Filing Deadline (“Motion”). The Commission grants EPE’s motion

for a four week extension of the deadline for the filing of its rate case, for the following reasons.

                                           DISCUSSION

         1.       On February 6, 2026, EPE filed its Motion for “an order granting EPE a variance

from the requirement that it file its rate case package no later than 150 days after the last day of

the Base Period.” 1 EPE sought the positions of parties to its most recent rate case, Case No. 20-

00104-UT, and no opposition was expressed by those parties. 2

         2.       EPE seeks a four-week extension of the deadline for its rate case filing to be

tendered, which would allow EPE to file its rate case on or before March 27, 2026, with a base

period ending on September 30, 2025. 3

         3.       On February 12, 2026, the Commission issued its Order Shortening Deadline for

Responses, which established that EPE’s Motion shall be addressed by the Commission as a




1 Motion (February 6, 2026) at 1.


2 Id. ¶ 18.


3 Id. ¶¶ 5-6, and ¶ 13.
 motion for extension of time, and ordered responses to EPE’s Motion to be filed by February 17,

2026. 4

          4.    No responses were filed to EPE’s unopposed Motion.

          5.    Rule 1.2.2.8(K) NMAC establishes that the time by which any person is required

to act under any rule may be extended by the commission or presiding officer for good cause.

          6.    In its Motion, EPE identified three challenges that have slowed its preparation of

its rate case application, 5 and stated that it is not clear whether EPE will be able to complete its

rate case package by February 27, 2026. 6 EPE asserted that “[r]ushing the rate case package

increases the possibility of an error or inaccuracy that will require time and resources to correct,”

and that “[i]t benefits all parties to avoid such errors and allow EPE time to make the rate package

as complete and accurate as possible. 7

          7.    The Commission finds good cause for granting EPE an extension of time for the

filing of its rate case package.

          IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

          A.    EPE’s motion for a four-week extension of the deadline for the filing of its rate case

package is GRANTED.

          B.    EPE shall file its rate case no later than March 27, 2026.

          C.    This Order is effective when signed.
